title: Committee of Supply – Head Q (Ministry of Communications and Information)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head Q (Ministry of Communications and Information)

sections.label: Top technology companies' market value
sections.summary: Seven of the world's top 10 companies by market capitalisation are technology companies, worth about US$6 trillion combined.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: By market capitalisation, seven out of the top 10 companies worldwide are technology companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Combined, these seven companies are worth about United States (US)$6 trillion.

sections.label: Digital trade agreements
sections.summary: Digital trade agreements, such as those concluded with New Zealand and Chile, could be helpful.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Perhaps, digital trade agreements, like the ones we just concluded with New Zealand and Chile, could be helpful.

sections.label: Computer Science and Data Science graduates
sections.summary: The question asks the number of Computer Science and Data Science graduates in local IHLs and whether Employment and S Passes could be issued if graduates are insufficient.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Can the Minister advise the number of Computer Science and Data Science graduates in our local institutes of higher learning (IHLs)?

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: If the number of graduates is insufficient to meet industry demand, could the Government allow for Employment and S Passes to be issued as an interim measure?

sections.label: Digital transformation for companies
sections.summary: Most, if not all, companies in Singapore agree digital transformation is a necessary step to survive.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Most, if not all, companies in Singapore would agree that digital transformation is no longer an option but a necessary step if they are to survive.

sections.label: SBF National Business Survey findings
sections.summary: SBF's National Business Survey 2019/2020 found SMEs know they need digital solutions for manpower costs and revenue, but costs are the biggest roadblock.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Earlier this year, SBF also released its National Business Survey 2019/2020, which found that SMEs know that they need to adopt digital solutions to tackle their top challenges of manpower costs and finding new and better ways to generate revenue, but costs remain the biggest roadblock.

sections.label: SME Go Digital Programme
sections.summary: The SME Go Digital Programme has helped over 4,000 companies implement digital solutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the SME Go Digital Programme has helped over 4,000 companies to implement digital solutions.

sections.label: ICM sector and PMET retraining
sections.summary: The ICM sector is a key growth sector in technology, and a stipend for mature PMETs undergoing retraining is suggested.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The Infocomm Media (ICM) sector is a key growth sector, particularly in technology, such as cybersecurity, Internet of Things, immersive media, data analytics and AI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: And would the Minster consider a stipend for mature PMETs who undergo retraining so that they are able to still take care of their families while they are doing so?

sections.label: Training and job placement
sections.summary: A request is made to go beyond the 20% salary support for six months to incentivise companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: They need to get the job first before they can get training, but they need the training to get the job.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask the Minister whether he can consider to go beyond what the Deputy Prime Minister announced in his Budget Statement of the 20% salary support for six months to further incentivise companies to take the first step.

sections.label: TeSA and TIPP training places
sections.summary: More than 93,000 TeSA training places were taken up since 2016, and 1,400 TIPP trainees completed as of October 2019.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: On 6 January this year, the Minister informed the House that more than 93,000 training places have been taken up or committed since the TechSkills Accelerator (TeSA) programme started in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: And as of October 2019, 1,400 trainees completed the Tech Immersion and Placement Programme (TIPP).

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Of the 93,000 TeSA places, how many have completed the programme, successfully found placement and stayed in the new jobs?

sections.label: Global reskilling need by 2030
sections.summary: One billion people globally need to be reskilled by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: One billion people globally need to be reskilled by 2030.

sections.label: Data centre electricity consumption
sections.summary: Data centres today consume about 2% of electricity worldwide.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Data centres today consume about 2% of electricity worldwide.

sections.label: PDPA and data portability
sections.summary: Individual data is increasingly easy to obtain, and the PDPA protects privacy but data portability concerns exist.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
sentences.text: With developments in technology ranging from facial recognition to online personality analysis, individual data is increasingly easy to obtain.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
sentences.text: We have the Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA) to protect individual privacy but there are also data portability concerns.

sections.label: Mandatory data protection officers under PDPA
sections.summary: PDPA 2012 requires every organisation to designate one or more individuals as data protection officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Under PDPA 2012, it is mandatory for every organisation to designate one or more individuals as data protection officers (DPOs).

sections.label: Employers, placement agencies, DPO training
sections.summary: The speaker looks forward to employers working with placement agencies to help PMET mid-career switchers become data protection professionals, and applauds the DPO Competency Framework and Training Roadmap published by PDPC on 17 July 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I look forward to seeing more employers collaborate with placement agencies, such as the Employment and Employability Institute, to help more PMET mid-career switchers, whether entering into the industry or being retained to be redeployed within the organisation, to transition into their new role as data protection professionals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I applaud the DPO Competency Framework and Training Roadmap which was published by the Personal Data Protection Commission (PDPC) on 17 July 2019.

sections.label: Facial recognition data storage limits
sections.summary: The speaker proposes that facial recognition data collected by private commercial entities not be stored more than 24 hours and not be linked to other information such as consumer buying pattern.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Chairman, may I propose that all facial recognition data collected by private commercial entities should not be stored for more than 24 hours?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Other than name, facial recognition data should not be linked to any other information, such as consumer buying pattern.

sections.label: 5G research, innovation ecosystem funding
sections.summary: In June 2019 Minister S Iswaran announced $40 million to develop the 5G research and innovation ecosystem, and the speaker asks about progress and 5G deployment plans given IMDA's 5G Call For Proposal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In June 2019, the Minister for Communications and Information, Mr S Iswaran, announced that the Government has set aside $40 million to develop the 5G research and innovation ecosystem, specifically to support 5G technology trials, open testbeds and enable research and development (R&D) in 5G.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What is the progress on Singapore's efforts to develop the 5G research and innovation ecosystem?

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Also, given IMDA's 5G Call For Proposal, what are our plans for 5G deployment?

sections.label: Survey on 5G cybercrime risks
sections.summary: An October 2019 survey by a US-based cybersecurity firm found 55% believed 5G deployment may enable more effective and destructive cybercrime and 54% thought it may give cybercriminals more opportunities to attack organisations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to a survey by a US-based cybersecurity firm, which was released in October 2019, 55% of those surveyed believe that 5G deployment may be avenues for more effective and destructive methods of cybercrime and another 54% thought it may give more opportunities for cybercriminals to attack the organisation.

sections.label: Ponemon survey on security attacks
sections.summary: In April last year the BBC reported a Ponemon Institute survey of security professionals across six countries finding 90% had been hit by at least one successful attack.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In April last year, the British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) carried a story that stated a survey of security professionals across six countries by the Ponemon Institute found that 90% had been hit by at least one successful attack.

sections.label: Singapore Cybersecurity Strategy document
sections.summary: In 2016, the Government published a document called Singapore's Cybersecurity Strategy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Chairman, in 2016, the Government published a document called "Singapore's Cybersecurity Strategy".

sections.label: Assessment of cybersecurity strategy implementation
sections.summary: It asks the Government's current assessment of the strategy's implementation and how far CSA contributed to grounding the four pillars.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: What is the Government's current assessment of the implementation of Singapore's cybersecurity strategy and how far has CSA contributed towards grounding the four pillars of the four strategies?

sections.label: Carbon Black survey on breaches
sections.summary: A 2019 Carbon Black report said 96% of surveyed Singapore companies experienced at least one breach in 12 months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, according to a report released on 1 October 2019 by a US-based cybersecurity firm, Carbon Black, 96% of surveyed companies in Singapore said they have experienced at least one cybersecurity breach in the past 12 months due to external cyberattacks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo
sentences.text: Of those that had experienced a cyberattack, 48% suffered negative financial impact while 83% reported damage to their reputation.

sections.label: Framework for large-scale cyberattack
sections.summary: It asks whether a similar framework exists to reduce and mitigate dangers of a large-scale national cyberattack.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo
sentences.text: In the event of a large-scale national cyberattack where computer and network viruses can spread speedily, is there a similar framework in place to reduce and mitigate the dangers of such an outbreak?

sections.label: Risks of cyberattacks
sections.summary: It states cyberattacks causing loss of personal data or attacks on critical OT systems could be disastrous, and state actors use cyberattacks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
sentences.text: In this highly connected world, cyberattacks resulting in loss of personal data and even more so attacks on our critical OT systems could be disastrous.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
sentences.text: Cyberattacks by state actors have also become a "weapon of choice", as can be seen in many countries.

sections.label: COVID-19 fake news and POFMA
sections.summary: It cites fake COVID-19 news in Singapore and states POFMA is a new law that is timely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
sentences.text: Fake news on COVID-19 have also surfaced here in Singapore. "Woodlands Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) station was closed on 28 January when it was actually fully operational" or "the Government giving $100 per day to every 'People's Republic of China (PRC) worker' for the 14-day period under the Leave of Absence, when it is to be given to eligible employees instead".

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
sentences.text: Fortunately for Singapore, we have a new law called the Protection from Online Falsehoods and Manipulation Act (POFMA) and, in retrospect, this new legislation is, indeed, timely.

sections.label: COVID-19 falsehoods hurting Singapore
sections.summary: The passage states that COVID-19 falsehoods have hurt Singapore, citing a false MRT closure, travel bans and a false death report.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, with the ongoing COVID-19 outbreak, we have seen destabilising falsehoods that have hurt our nation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
sentences.text: These range from the false closure of Woodlands MRT station; seven countries banning travel to Singapore; to an online falsehood regarding the death of a man in Singapore from COVID-19, when no such death had occurred.

sections.label: Testing POFMA and information infrastructure
sections.summary: The speaker asks how the Government has sharpened communication and POFMA capacities against online falsehoods amid COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: When this House passed POFMA in May last year, a mysterious yet highly contagious disease like COVID-19 was but a black swan to be avoided.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But the crisis now presents us with a valuable opportunity to test the mettle of our information infrastructures, including official communication channels, public education efforts and regulatory measures, such as POFMA.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the wake of COVID-19, therefore, I would like to ask how the Government has sharpened its ability to communicate quickly and effectively to all demographic groups in a digitalised world with porous information boundaries.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Importantly, can the ministry share how our capacities to cope with online falsehoods have been stretched and what measures will we take to reinforce them?

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With specific regard to POFMA and its application, can we conduct more systematic assessments of the effects of the targeted and general corrections approach?

sections.label: DORSCON Orange announcement leak
sections.summary: The speaker asks how information flow can be tightened to avoid future leaks, citing the DORSCON Orange leak.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
sentences.text: To contextualise my questions, I am concerned that Singapore's movement to DORSCON Orange was leaked ahead of its official announcement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
sentences.text: First, how can we tighten the information flow to avoid any future leaks?

sections.label: COVID-19 communication versus H1N1 and SARS
sections.summary: The speaker asks how effective COVID-19 communication was compared to H1N1 and SARS, and whether WhatsApp Gov.sg will continue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
sentences.text: Third, how effective and different were the Government's efforts in communicating to Singaporeans during this COVID-19 crisis, in comparison to our response to Hemagglutinin type 1 and Neuraminidase type 1 (H1N1) and SARS?

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
sentences.text: Lastly, will the Government continue to make use of the WhatsApp channel, such as Gov.sg?

sections.label: POFMA limits on messaging and scams
sections.summary: The passage states POFMA has limitations, particularly for fake news spread through messaging services and for scams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: There is legislation, such as POFMA, that can help the Government take action against online fake news.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: But this has its limitations, particularly in the context of: one, fake news that spreads through messaging services rather than online; and two, scams which can take advantage of people's trusting nature.

sections.label: Singapore uses POFMA correction orders
sections.summary: The passage states Singapore issues POFMA correction orders for deliberate COVID-19 falsehoods, unlike countries that arrest perpetrators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While some countries have taken strong positions on the deliberate spread of falsehood regarding COVID-19 by even arresting the perpetrators, the Singapore Government has taken on a different position by issuing correction orders under POFMA.

sections.label: FTA TV and OTT trends
sections.summary: A 2018 Nielsen report found about 3.4 million people in Singapore watched FTA TV weekly, while on-demand OTT consumption trended upward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Although the Nielsen Singapore Media Index Report released in late 2018 found that approximately 3.4 million people in Singapore continued to tune in to FTA TV channels on a weekly basis, the same report also highlighted that there is an upward trend of people consuming on-demand OTT media services.

sections.label: Multilingual WhatsApp service scaling
sections.summary: The multilingual WhatsApp service introduced during the COVID-19 outbreak has been useful and should be scaled up for all public information.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: The multilingual WhatsApp service recently introduced during this COVID-19 outbreak has been most useful.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: We should scale up this multilingual capability to enable all Singaporeans to access all public information in a timely manner.

sections.label: Local translation project idea
sections.summary: A speaker suggests a local translation project for Singapore's multicultural and multilingual society, put online or enhanced with technology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Somehow, I have a thought – what if we have a local project, given our multicultural and multilingual society, a local translation project and then, put it online or using technology to enhance it, it would be wonderful.

sections.label: US print and e-book reading
sections.summary: Pew Research Centre data show US adults reading print books fell from 71% in 2011 to 65%, while e-book reading rose from 17% to 25% in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
sentences.text: According	to	Pew	Research	Centre, the percentage of US adults that have used or read a print book in the past 12 months has fallen from 71% in 2011 to 65% last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
sentences.text: Conversely, the percentage of US adults that have read an e-book in the past 12 months has increased from 17% in 2011 to 25% in 2019.

sections.label: E-library borrowing and future libraries
sections.summary: E-library borrowing via apps like Overdrive is increasingly common, so future libraries' strategic positioning needs review as community nodes, social spaces or lifelong learning venues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
sentences.text: Borrowing from e-libraries using various applications, such as Overdrive, is also increasingly common.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
sentences.text: Bearing this in mind, there is a need to review the strategic positioning of future libraries, possibly as nodes to foster community or as common spaces for citizens to socialise or as venues to promote lifelong learning.

sections.label: Southeast Asia digital economy investment
sections.summary: Southeast Asia's digital economy will treble to US$300 billion by 2025, and the $8 billion Transform and Grow package invests in business innovation and people's skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: In Southeast Asia alone, the digital economy will treble to US$300 billion by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: With the $8 billion Transform and Grow package in the Budget, we are investing significantly in the innovation capacity of our businesses and the skills of our people, so that they can fully realise these benefits.

sections.label: Digital Economy Agreements
sections.summary: Singapore pursues Digital Economy Agreements with Australia, Chile and New Zealand to support open digital trade and cross-border digital payments.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Our goal and our interest is to work with like-minded partners to ensure an open digital trade architecture and to guard against a new kind of protectionism.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: That is why Singapore is actively pursuing Digital Economy Agreements (DEAs) with countries like Australia, Chile and New Zealand.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: These agreements will benefit businesses by providing for secure data flows and seamless cross-border digital payments.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: For example, when DEAs establish e-invoicing systems that are interoperable across borders, enterprises can transact at a lower cost with their international business partners because of faster invoice processing and payment.

sections.label: 5G spectrum submissions
sections.summary: IMDA received three 5G submissions from telcos and aims to announce the spectrum award by mid-2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: At the close of CFP on 17 February, IMDA had received three submissions from the incumbent telecommunications companies (telcos) – one each from Singtel and TPG, as well as a joint submission from StarHub and M1.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: IMDA is evaluating the proposals and aims to announce the award of the 5G spectrum by mid-2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: We are on track to commence 5G deployment this year, achieve substantial coverage in the next two years, and nationwide standalone coverage by 2025.

sections.label: Nationwide parcel locker network
sections.summary: Singapore will deploy a nationwide parcel locker network because doorstep delivery of growing parcel volumes is unsustainable.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: In Singapore, around 200,000 parcels are delivered daily, with e-commerce projected to grow at 12% to 20% annually over the next five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, it is neither productive nor sustainable for this growing volume of packages to all be delivered to the doorstep.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And that is why we have decided to deploy a nationwide parcel locker network.

sections.label: IDPs for ITM sectors
sections.summary: The Government will develop IDPs and pre-approve more digital solutions to cover all 23 ITM sectors, up from 10.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Building on this momentum, the Government will develop IDPs and pre-approve more digital solutions to cover all 23 Industry Transformation Map (ITM) sectors, up from the current 10.

sections.label: Training places and job retention
sections.summary: About 100,000 training places have been committed since April 2016, and 90% of long-form course trainees stayed in jobs a year later.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Since its launch in April 2016, about 100,000 training places have been committed, so a progress from the number I gave earlier this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: For the CLT programme and Tech Immersion and Placement Programme (TIPP), which are long-form courses, in other words, they are courses over a long duration and therefore go deeper, 90% of trainees successfully stayed in the job a year after the completion of training.

sections.label: Programme funding and placements
sections.summary: The programme has been set aside $70 million, aiming to place 2,000 more Singaporeans in companies over two to three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: For a start, we have set aside $70 million for this programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Over the next two to three years, we aim to place a further 2,000 Singaporeans in companies through this programme.

sections.label: Libraries plan and Digital Defence
sections.summary: A library held over 360 programmes in a year, forming the model for a five-year Libraries and Archives Plan, and Digital Defence became Total Defence's sixth pillar.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: In just one year since its opening in January last year, it has held over 360 programmes, more than a third of them run by members of the community, in other words, volunteers.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: These unique partnerships form the model for the Libraries and Archives Plan (LAP25), and this goes to the point that Mr Cedric Foo raised.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: This is a five-year strategic plan for our libraries and archives.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: But to fully derive the benefits of digitalisation, we must protect ourselves from the threats in the digital domain.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: That is why we have instituted Digital Defence as the sixth pillar of Total Defence to underscore the importance of ensuring that digital spaces where we increasingly interact, transact and rely on for information are safe, secure and trustworthy.

sections.label: Safer Cyberspace and PDPA review
sections.summary: A Safer Cyberspace Masterplan will launch this year, and the PDPA is being reviewed to balance business data needs with consumer protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Later this year, we will also launch a Safer Cyberspace Masterplan to proactively monitor and prevent cyber threats and cybercrime, implement baseline security standards and increase the adoption of these safeguards by enterprises and citizens.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Data protection also takes on added importance in this context.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: That is why we are reviewing the PDPA to support, on the one hand, the legitimate needs of businesses to harness data for innovative products and services, while protecting consumers' interests and increasing the accountability of organisations.

sections.label: POFMA correction orders
sections.summary: POFMA correction orders exposed falsehoods by placing the truth alongside, and firmer levers were used against a recalcitrant Facebook page.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: POFMA correction orders were used to swiftly expose them by placing the truth alongside.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Firmer levers were used when a recalcitrant Facebook page repeatedly posted falsehoods and refused to carry any corrections.

sections.label: More investment in PSB
sections.summary: The Government will invest more in PSB to ensure the medium's quality and relevance to Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The Government will, therefore, invest more in PSB to ensure the quality and relevance to Singaporeans of this important medium.

sections.label: COVID-19 public information updates
sections.summary: Digital display panels and the Gov.sg WhatsApp channel gave near real-time updates, with over 650,000 new subscribers in five weeks and over 80% of polled residents satisfied.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Digital display panels in Housing and Development Board (HDB) estates and Gov.sg WhatsApp channel have given almost real-time updates to Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: We have seen a huge surge in subscribers of over 650,000 in just five weeks to gov.sg's WhatsApp service which issues regular messages in the four official languages.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: From mid to late February, the feedback unit Reaching Everyone for Active Citizenry @ Home (REACH) conducted an online poll to understand public sentiments and more than 80% of Singaporeans or Singapore residents who were polled indicated that the Government had provided sufficient information about the COVID-19 situation.

sections.label: CII sector recommendation progress
sections.summary: The Energy, Infocomm, Security and Emergency sectors fully implemented all recommendations or compensating controls, while other sectors implemented measures for 70% to 90% of their CIIs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: To date, the Energy, Infocomm, Security and Emergency sectors have fully implemented all the recommendations or compensating controls.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Other sectors have made good progress and implemented measures for between 70% and 90% of their CIIs.

sections.label: OT cybersecurity masterplan launch
sections.summary: CSA launched the OT Masterplan in October last year to raise awareness and competencies in OT cybersecurity.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: To address this, CSA has launched the OT Masterplan in October last year to raise awareness and competencies in OT cybersecurity.

sections.label: Cybersecurity labelling for home devices
sections.summary: CSA will launch the Cybersecurity Labelling Scheme for home routers and smart home hubs, and IMDA will set minimum security requirements for home routers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Going forward, CSA will be launching the Cybersecurity Labelling Scheme (CLS) for home routers and smart home hubs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: IMDA will be setting minimum security requirements for home routers.

sections.label: Data portability obligation in PDPA
sections.summary: Singapore will introduce a new Data Portability Obligation in the PDPA so individuals can have their data transmitted between organisations in a commonly used format.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: This network of partnerships that Singapore has and our Digital Economy Agreements (DEAs) will also facilitate cross-border interoperability and collaboration.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We will introduce a new Data Portability Obligation in the Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA) so that individuals can have their data transmitted between organisations in a commonly used format.

sections.label: Guides on biometric technology use
sections.summary: The PDPC and the Government Data Office will publish guides this year on the responsible use of biometric technology.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: In order to promote the responsible use of facial recognition technologies, the Personal Data Protection Commission (PDPC) and the Government Data Office will publish guides on the responsible use of biometric technology this year.

sections.label: Proposed PDPA amendments review
sections.summary: The review proposes obligating organisations to notify affected individuals and PDPC of significant data breaches, strengthening PDPC's enforcement powers, and instilling accountability practices like risk assessments.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: The key proposed amendments under this review include: (a) obligating organisations to notify affected individuals and PDPC of significant data breaches; (b) strengthening PDPC's enforcement powers; and (c) instilling accountability practices like risk assessments for organisations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We plan to amend the PDPA later this year.

sections.label: Blocking international scam calls
sections.summary: IMDA worked with telcos to block international scammers spoofing commonly spoofed numbers, and will require a "+" prefix for all overseas calls.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: IMDA has worked with the telcos to block international scammers from making their phone call look like they are coming from commonly spoofed numbers, such as 999 and 995.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We will move on to introduce measures to stop international scammers from trying to spoof numbers that look like they are a local number, targeting our citizens by introducing a requirement to have the "+" symbol as a prefix for all overseas calls.

sections.label: Inter-Ministry Committee on Scams
sections.summary: MCI will work with other agencies in the new Inter-Ministry Committee on Scams announced by MHA to tackle the problem.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: MCI will work closely with other agencies in the newly formed Inter-Ministry Committee on Scams announced by MHA to strengthen our collective efforts to tackle this problem.

sections.label: Select Committee fact-checking recommendations
sections.summary: The Select Committee on Deliberate Online Falsehoods recommended Government support for fact-checking initiatives and stronger public education.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: The Select Committee on Deliberate Online Falsehoods recommended for the Government to support fact-checking initiatives and strengthen public education to build an informed and discerning citizenry.

sections.label: PDPC training 500 DPOs
sections.summary: PDPC will collaborate with partners such as NTUC to roll out courses and train 500 DPOs in the first year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: PDPC will collaborate with partners, such as NTUC, to roll out additional courses and targets to train 500 DPOs in the first year.

sections.label: SG Cyber Talent initiative
sections.summary: CSA is launching SG Cyber Talent to reach over 20,000 individuals in three years, with two new programmes this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: CSA is launching the SG Cyber Talent initiative to reach out to more than 20,000 individuals over three years through existing and new programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Under the SG Cyber Talent programme, CSA will introduce two new programmes this year.

sections.label: CSA Academy global partner training
sections.summary: CSA Academy has worked with global partners since 2018 to train CSA and CII sectors, training about 200 professionals to date.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: CSA Academy has also been working with global partners to provide intermediate and advanced training for CSA, as well as for the CII sectors since 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: To date, the Academy has trained about 200 professionals.

sections.label: Consumer complaints December 2019 fall
sections.summary: Consumer complaints fell by about 40% in December 2019 compared to 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Consumer complaints fell by about 40% in December 2019 compared to 2018.

sections.label: Nationwide locker station deployment
sections.summary: IMDA will launch 1,000 locker stations in HDB estates, MRT stations and Community Centres by end of 2022, aiming for one within five minutes' walk of every HDB block.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Building on the success of the Locker Alliance pilot, IMDA will launch a nationwide deployment of 1,000 locker stations in HDB estates, MRT stations and Community Centres by the end of 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The goal is to place a locker station around five minutes' walk from every HDB block.

sections.label: Media mentorship programmes
sections.summary: Mentorship programmes WritersLab, ProducersLab and the Story Lab Apprenticeship will benefit over 200 media professionals over the next two years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Mentorship programmes like WritersLab, ProducersLab and the Story Lab Apprenticeship also help media professionals sharpen their tools of the trade.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: These programmes will benefit over 200 media professionals over the next two years.

sections.label: SG Ambassadors engage seniors
sections.summary: 3,000 Silver Generation Ambassadors actively engage seniors regarding the Merdeka Generation Package.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: For example, 3,000 Silver Generation (SG) Ambassadors actively engage seniors with regard to the Merdeka Generation Package (MGP).

sections.label: MCI Translation Department repositioned
sections.summary: MCI will reposition its Translation Department as the whole-of-Government Centre of Excellence for Translation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: MCI is now ready to consolidate these moves.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We will signal a higher level of aspiration, by repositioning MCI's TD as the whole-of-Government Centre of Excellence for Translation.

sections.label: SG Translate supports COVID-19 communications
sections.summary: The machine translation engine SG Translate has supported translation of public communications materials in vernacular languages in the national fight against COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: In the national fight against COVID-19, our machine translation engine, known as SG Translate, has been supporting the translation of public communications materials in vernacular languages.

sections.label: SG Translate Together pilot launch
sections.summary: MCI is launching a new pilot project, SG Translate Together, to rally Singaporeans to improve SG Translate.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We fully agree partnerships are important to share knowledge and expertise.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: That is why MCI is launching a new pilot project, SG Translate Together, to rally Singaporeans to improve SG Translate.

sections.label: Legal Deposit collection items
sections.summary: The Legal Deposit collection holds over 1.37 million items contributed by publishers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: In total, the Legal Deposit collection has more than 1.37 million items contributed by publishers.

sections.label: Home Access Programme broadband subsidy
sections.summary: The Home Access Programme has subsidised broadband for over 14,000 low-income households.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: To support low-income Singaporeans, the Home Access Programme has subsidised broadband for over 14,000 households.

sections.label: Enhanced Home Access Programme
sections.summary: IMDA will enhance the Home Access Programme from April, partnering M1, MyRepublic and NetLink Trust to benefit 10,000 more households over three years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: To benefit more low-income households, IMDA will enhance the Home Access Programme from April.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: IMDA will partner M1, MyRepublic Limited and NetLink Trust to defray the cost of broadband for low-income households, while offering faster broadband speeds.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: IMDA will also offer a wider range of devices, giving households the choice of either a subsidised smartphone or tablet.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We aim to benefit 10,000 more low-income households over three years.

sections.label: Thousand lockers deployment
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes the deployment of a thousand lockers across Singapore, especially within five minutes of an HDB block.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I welcome the deployment of the thousand lockers across Singapore, particularly to have it located within five minutes of an HDB block.

sections.label: New unit under MCI or MOT
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Ministry can study setting up a new unit or entity under MCI or MOT, similar to HTX.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
sentences.text: Can the Ministry study the possibility of setting up a new unit or an entity under either MCI or the Ministry of Transport (MOT), similar to Home Team Science and Technology Agency (HTX) under MHA.

sections.label: Child computer and broadband access
sections.summary: The question asks whether no child in a Singapore school will lack a computer and broadband access if their family cannot afford one.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
sentences.text: Chairman, I would like to ask Senior Minister of State Sim Ann whether or not we can confidently say that no child in a Singapore school will be without a computer and broadband access if their family cannot afford one.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: This is a goal shared by MCI as well as MOE.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: We will do our part in terms of ensuring that low-income households are able to have home access.

sections.label: POFMA and messaging app falsehoods
sections.summary: POFMA handles online falsehoods, but Correction Orders do not work effectively for falsehoods spread through messaging apps like WhatsApp during COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: Chairman, one of the points I mentioned was that POFMA is very useful in handling online falsehoods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: But in the COVID-19 situation, one of the things we realised is that a lot of the falsehoods spread through messaging apps, such as WhatsApp, for which the Correction Orders in POFMA would not work effectively.

sections.label: gov.sg WhatsApp service
sections.summary: This was one reason the speaker was keen to move on the gov.sg WhatsApp service.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, without wanting to prolong that discussion on POFMA, let me just say that, I think, essentially this is one of the reasons why we were very keen to move on the gov.sg WhatsApp service.

sections.label: POFMA regulation of WhatsApp platforms
sections.summary: WhatsApp's end-to-end encryption poses a different POFMA challenge, so the approach accounts for platform variations, including WhatsApp and Facebook.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: In terms of the actual mechanisms for dealing with platforms like WhatsApp because they have end-to-end encryption and so they pose a different kind of challenge in terms of the POFMA regulation compared to some of the other platforms.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: As we said during the POFMA debate, we are taking an approach which takes into account the variations across different platforms and that includes WhatsApp and Facebook whom we are engaging in an ongoing discussion.
